summary.text: John Lemondes is the incumbent Republican and Conservative Party candidate for New York State Assembly District 126 in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A retired Army colonel and livestock farmer from LaFayette, he was first elected to the Assembly in 2020.

paragraphs.text: Lemondes served 27 years in the U.S. Army, including combat operations in Iraq and Afghanistan, and retired as a Colonel in 2014, according to his official biography.
His service included leading the U.S. Army Chemical Materials Agency team responsible for meeting treaty obligations to the Organization for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons.

After retiring from the Army, he and his family began operating a diversified livestock farm in LaFayette while he worked in the defense industry on naval and Marine Corps radar platforms, and he later served as president of the New York Farmer Veteran Coalition.
Lemondes was elected to the Assembly on November 3, 2020, and was re-elected in 2022; after redistricting his district contains parts of Onondaga and Cayuga counties.
He is a member of the Agriculture, Banks, Corporations, Authorities and Commissions, Economic Development, and Environmental Conservation committees.
His official biography lists lower taxes, job creation, agriculture, Second Amendment rights and support for veterans and law enforcement among his priorities.
